text:
maria: heads-up — kicking off planning for sharded telemetry migration. goal: add an `epoch` column to telemetry events so we can rotate partitioning without locking route ids. want minimal console/read impact and a clear rollback playbook.

jamal: quick q — why add `epoch` instead of reusing/renaming `partition_id`?

maria: good callout. `partition_id` is too overloaded today. `epoch` gives us a versioned namespace: new writes stamped with epoch=N, reads can query multiple epochs during cutover. makes backfills and rollbacks explicit.

dmitri: timeline? do we need a big maintenance window?

maria: propose: canary write-only for 2h (thurs 03:00 UTC) -> staged read-adapter behind FF for 24h -> full cutover fri 01:00 UTC with 1h verification window. rollback cap: stop writes, flip adapter, resume.

olivia: console read paths will need an adapter that merges epochs. can we do an adapter that prefers latest epoch but falls back to older ones?

maria: yes: adapter will `COALESCE(latest_epoch.row, legacy.row)` semantics. feature flag to gate the adapter. fallback query pattern: 
```
-- read adapter sketch
SELECT * FROM telemetry
WHERE route_id = $1
  AND (epoch = current_epoch OR epoch IS NULL)
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

sophie: dashboards: freeze automation that depends on counts for 48h around cutover. i'll add an incident page and update on-call playbook. also need to update docs on alerting for p50/p95 token processing.

jamal: safety checklist? what do we run pre/post?

maria: posting checklist now: 
- pre-canary: shadow dualwrite enabled for 24h, verify duplicate rates < 0.01%
- canary: enable epoch header on a small tenant subset (10 tenants), monitor consumer lag and p95 API latency
- pre-cutover: run backfill sizing estimate for older epochs (ETA + bytes)
- cutover: enable adapter FF, flip routing for writes to epoch=N, watch for duplicate keys and consumer errors
- verification: traffic QPS stable, consumer lag < 5m, error rate < 0.1%
- rollback: stop writes to epoch=N, re-enable legacy writes, disable adapter FF, run a short cleanup job to mark incomplete records

jamal: any concrete queries we can use to detect issues?

maria: yes — run these before canary and during: 
```
-- duplicate route_id counts across epochs
SELECT route_id, COUNT(DISTINCT epoch) as epoch_count
FROM telemetry
WHERE route_id IN (SELECT route_id FROM canary_tenants)
GROUP BY route_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT epoch) > 1
LIMIT 20;

-- detect orphaned newer epochs (no legacy row)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telemetry t
WHERE t.epoch = current_epoch
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM telemetry legacy
    WHERE legacy.route_id = t.route_id AND (legacy.epoch IS NULL OR legacy.epoch = current_epoch - 1)
  );
```

dmitri: also add consumer-side checks: kafka consumer lag, reprocessing error rate. I'll add a small probe that alerts if consumer exceptions > 5 in 5m.

canary-bot: scheduled canary write for tenant group "gc-canary" at 2026-03-28T03:00:00Z.

olivia: read adapter PR needs to include a query plan guard — we can't do full-table epoch scans. add index on (route_id, epoch, timestamp) first.

maria: agreed. dba approved `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY telemetry_route_epoch_ts_idx ON telemetry (route_id, epoch, timestamp DESC);`

jamal: backfill approach? we can't rewrite everything at once.

maria: plan: incremental async backfill that writes epoch for legacy rows but keeps legacy read semantics until cutover. backfill concurrency controlled by job queue to keep DB load < 20% of peak. backfill job idempotent and rate-limited.

sophie: ops comms — i'll craft the email and slack banners: include expected read fuzziness and dashboard freeze. also will update the runbook with rollback signals.

dmitri: rollback signals? what thresholds will flip rollback?

maria: proposed automatic rollback triggers: 
- consumer error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m
- read p95 increased > 2x baseline for 15m
- >1% of canary tenants see missing data for >5m
If any triggers fire, runbook instructs to stop writes to new epoch and roll adapter back.

olivia: add a quick manual query to confirm adapter state: 
```
SELECT route_id, epoch, count(*) FROM telemetry
WHERE route_id IN (SELECT route_id FROM canary_tenants)
GROUP BY route_id, epoch
ORDER BY route_id, epoch DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

maria: post-cutover: we will keep legacy epoch=null rows for 7 days, then run a cleanup job to merge duplicates. cleanup job will be opted-in per-tenant for first month.

jamal: testing matrix? unit + staging + prod canary?

maria: yes: unit tests for adapter logic, staging with sampled traffic replay, prod canary on 10 tenants, then 100 tenants ramp.

canary-bot: canary finished: write probe OK for group "gc-canary" (0 errors, 120 events)

olivia: PRs look good. please add `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for the adapter query in the PR description so we can watch it in prod.

sophie: added support on-call checklist and note for finance to expect slight metric variance in billing exports for cutover window.

maria: action items: 
- @dmitri create index migration job and safety rollback script (ETA: today EOD)
- @jamal add consumer lag probe + alert (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- @olivia open read-adapter PR with explain and FF flags (ETA: tomorrow)
- @sophie post comms and freeze dashboards (ETA: tomorrow noon)
- I'll open the backfill controller PR (ETA: Wed)

jamal: +1. please make sure runbook includes `psql` snippets to cut adapter flags quickly.

maria: will add. also attaching short `kubectl` snippet for feature flag flip: 
```
# flip adapter flag in configmap
kubectl -n infra patch configmap feature-flags --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/epoch_adapter","value":"true"}]'
```

dmitri: once index create runs, I'll monitor replication lag. I'll post metrics in #incidents channel if anything spikes.

maria: thanks all — i'll schedule a short dry-run with the canary group tomorrow. will post final cutover timeline once the PRs land.

canary-bot: reminder: dry-run scheduled 2026-03-27T03:00:00Z for tenant group "gc-canary".
